note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers, only the worker has a complete description; measurements follow the original ranges.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: From A. spiculatus it differs in that the latter is slightly larger, has the fourth marginal tooth of the left mandible not touching the molar prominence, the enteric valve ridges taper-ellipsoid rather than waisted and of varying degree of sclerotization, with fewer, straight conical spines on ridges one and three, and the valve bilaterally symmetrical. From A. mbalmayoensis it differs as described under that species: the latter is much larger, without conspicuous stout setae on the fore coxa, and differs in the enteric valve spines and in the symmetry of the valve.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum, pronotum and legs all yellowish white, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule short-oval, nearly circular, setae sparse, projecting, the longest setae arranged regularly and symmetrically. Fontanelle absent. Anterior surface of the fore coxa with 4 or more stout setae arranged in rows or groups; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third well developed, at least one-half the length of the others. Left mandible: first marginal tooth nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth as long as that of the first marginal tooth, the fourth marginal tooth just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.642—0.647 mm; pronotum width 0.412—0.436 mm, length 0.183—0.191 mm; hind tibia length 0.624—0.629 mm; fore tibia length 0.525—0.531 mm; left mandible index 0.802—0.903, right mandible index 1.049—1.163.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally below the nerve cord; the first hindgut segment is rather short, up to 8 times as long as its proximal width, tubular throughout; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the right of the heart (dorsal view) or to the left of the nerve cord (ventral view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is smaller than the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are markedly waisted at the base of the apical spines and then widen, with weakly sclerotized, pale yellow or yellow ends; the primary rows bear very long tapering spines, at most 15—20 on ridge one, 1—9 on ridges two and four, and 15 to more than 20 on ridge three; the longest are curved but evenly tapering, longer than the narrowest width at the base of the apical spines of ridge three; the symmetry is nearly three-radiate, with the intercalary ridges reduced; the secondary rows bear conspicuous spines on one or more ridges.
